messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Extracting Linear Combinations of INLA Features
parts:
Dear Alfred,

I prefer to use inla.make.lincombs(). It takes a named list. The names must be identical to the name of the parameter. In case of a fixed effect, use a vector (one element per contrast). In case of a random effect, use a matrix (one row per contrast, one column for each random effect index).
You can name the contrasts by setting names to the output of inla.make.lincombs().

Best regards,

Op do 15 aug. 2019 om 19:51 schreef 'Alfred' via R-inla discussion group <r-inla-disc...@googlegroups.com>:
Hello,

I have built a price elasticity model (regressing logQuantity on logPrice and other variables). Among many other variables, I have included logPrice and interactions between logPrice and categorical variables (e.g., colour of t-shirt). I also have a random slope for each product using f(ProductName, logPrice, model = 'iid'). I am trying to extract the posterior distribution of the elasticity for each individual product. This would include the estimate of the fixed logPrice effect, all relevant interactions (varies by product), and the random slope estimate.

I have read the FAQ section on linear combinations but am not sure how to specify the linear combinations that involve interaction effects (do I specify the names of the interactions? do I code with 1s and 0s or the level names?), the random effect/fixed effect interaction, and how to only include the elasticity-related terms (i.e., I also have a fixed intercept for each product and the uncertainty in that is irrelevant for this task).

Any help with the API would be much appreciated! Thanks!
